messages:
Anna (sales): Heads up — FinServX Qs on commit sizing. They expect two concurrent profiles at peak: 1) short chat ~250 rps, avg 40 tokens, SLO 95th <300ms. 2) long synthesis ~30 rps, avg 800 tokens, SLO 95th <1s. Asking whether to push them to a reserved GPU commit or rely on burst credits + autoscale. Need a quick sketch of GPU counts + fallback policy by EOD.
Devon (eng): Which model variant are they planning to run?
Anna (sales): They want rw-infer-3b-q4 (we recommended quantized 3B) for parity with current proofs.
Michael (infra): Quick back-of-envelope: short chat: 250 rps * 40 tok = 10k tok/s. long synth: 30 rps * 800 tok = 24k tok/s. total ~34k tok/s at peak.
Michael (infra): Bench notes: rw-infer-3b-q4 -> ~9k tok/s per GPU for mixed short sequences; long decode-heavy flows drop to ~3k tok/s per GPU effective when avg seq ~800. So capacity needs to consider mix.
Michael (infra): Conservative GPU estimate: handle longs: 24k / 3k ≈ 8 GPUs. Shorts distributed across same pool give 10k / 9k ≈ 2 GPUs. Because of mixed peaks and headroom, plan for 10 GPUs reserved to keep 95th latency headroom + room for autoscale smoothing.
Devon (eng): If we want cost-limited option, we can reserve 6 GPUs and rely on burst credits/autoscale to cover spikes (spare 4 GPUs worth). Need to decide risk tolerance: preheat latency vs cost.
Sara (sre): Pricing note for presales: reserved GPUs get a discount ~30% vs on-demand; burst credits priced separately and useful for <4hr/day spikes. For FinServX expected daily pattern?
Anna (sales): They said typical diurnal with 2hr morning spike and occasional batch synths. Not continuous peak.
Devon (eng): Autoscale policy I propose (for the Dedicated/reserved mix):
```
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  reserved_replicas: 6   # guaranteed commit
  max_replicas: 12
  target_rps_per_replica: 40
  token_budget_per_replica: 9000
  kv_cache_warmup: true
  preheat_policy: 10m   # pre-start replicas 10m before expected window
  fallback_model: rw-infer-1b-q4
```
Devon (eng): Key ideas: keep a small always-on pool to preserve KV cache and reduce cold-starts, reserve a baseline commit for predictability, allow burst to max if budget/credits available. Fallback to 1B-quantized model for graceful degradation under sustained oversubscription.
Michael (infra): Operational concerns: KV cache warmup matters for long sequences where prefix reuse exists — plan automated prewarm during SLA windows. Also preallocate token buckets so autoscaler isn't reactive per-request.
Anna (sales): FinServX legal wants an SLA ladder — if we fail 95th we need documented failover (model fallback + traffic shaping). Is that OK?
Sara (sre): That's standard. We can commit to model fallback + progressive rate-limit (first shed non-critical batch synth jobs) and document the runbook. Also add AZ fallback if a single AZ degrades.
Michael (infra): Quick note about billing: if we reserve 6 GPUs, enable burst credits for the other 6 to cover the morning 2hr spike — that keeps committed cost reasonable and meets spike SLOs in practice.
Anna (sales): Nice. Can someone summarize into a short recommendation I can send to the customer? I need a sharp ask: recommended reserved GPUs, expected headroom, fallback policy, and cost tradeoffs.
Devon (eng): TL;DR to send: reserve 6 GPUs (commit) with burst-capacity to reach 12 GPUs during peak. Configure autoscale min_replicas 2, max_replicas 12, target_rps_per_replica 40, prewarm KV cache 10m before window. Fallback: rw-infer-1b-q4 and staged rate-limiting for non-critical jobs. Expect steady-state cost ≈ reserved-6 price, burst costs only during spikes.
Anna (sales): Perfect. I'll draft and include the runbook snippet. Thanks team :thumbsup:
OpsBot: Preheat job scheduled for FinServX trial window 2026-04-02 08:50 UTC (prewarm 10m) :rocket:
Anna (sales): Logging that action in the customer packet. Follow-ups: 1) Sara to confirm pricing delta for reserved-6 vs reserved-10; 2) Michael to produce perf curves for rw-infer-3b-q4 at seq lengths 40/800.
Sara (sre): On it, will DM numbers by EOD.
Michael (infra): Will run perf sweep and post results here by EOD.
Anna (sales): Thanks — will close out with customer after we have the numbers.
